# packages

```{r packages}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggpubr)
library(survival)
library(dplyr)
library(lme4)

# ---- plotting helpers (ggplot2 only) ----
# survminer's ggsurvplot() and ggforest() draw blank panels under ggplot2 >= 4.0 (survminer issue #694),
# so the Kaplan-Meier curves, risk tables and hazard-ratio plots are drawn with ggplot2 directly.

# Kaplan-Meier curves (step lines, 95% CI bands, censoring marks) + number-at-risk table.
# Returns list(plot, table) like ggsurvplot(), so the multi-panel figures below are built the same way.
# labels: named vector, factor level -> display label (in plotting order)
km_plot <- function(fit, pval, palette, title, labels, legend_title, xmax = 36, by = 5) {
  lev <- sub("^.*=", "", names(fit$strata))
  st  <- factor(rep(lev, fit$strata), levels = lev)
  d <- data.frame(level = st, time = fit$time, surv = fit$surv, lower = fit$lower, upper = fit$upper,
                  n.censor = fit$n.censor)
  d <- rbind(data.frame(level = factor(lev, levels = lev), time = 0, surv = 1, lower = 1, upper = 1, n.censor = 0), d)
  d <- d[order(d$level, d$time), ]
  d$group <- factor(labels[as.character(d$level)], levels = labels)
  # step-shaped confidence band: one rectangle per interval between event times
  d <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(d, d$level), function(x) { x$time_end <- c(x$time[-1], x$time[nrow(x)]); x }))
  d$lower[is.na(d$lower)] <- d$surv[is.na(d$lower)]; d$upper[is.na(d$upper)] <- d$surv[is.na(d$upper)]
  cols <- setNames(palette, labels)
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = time, y = surv, colour = group)) +
    geom_rect(aes(xmin = time, xmax = time_end, ymin = lower, ymax = upper, fill = group),
              colour = NA, alpha = 0.25, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    geom_step(linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_point(data = d[d$n.censor > 0, ], shape = 3, size = 2, show.legend = FALSE) +
    annotate("text", x = 1, y = 0.08, label = pval, hjust = 0, size = 4.5) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = cols, name = legend_title) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = cols, name = legend_title) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, xmax), breaks = seq(0, xmax, by), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.03, 0.02))) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.03, 0.02))) +
    labs(x = "Days", y = "Survival Probability", title = title) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "top", plot.title = element_text(face = "italic")) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2), fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
  # number at risk at each axis break
  tt <- seq(0, xmax, by)
  sm <- summary(fit, times = tt, extend = TRUE)
  r <- data.frame(level = sub("^.*=", "", as.character(sm$strata)), time = sm$time, n = sm$n.risk)
  r$group <- factor(labels[r$level], levels = rev(labels))
  tab <- ggplot(r, aes(x = time, y = group, label = n, colour = group)) +
    geom_text(size = 3.8, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = cols) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, xmax), breaks = tt, expand = expansion(mult = c(0.03, 0.02))) +
    labs(x = "Days", y = NULL, title = "Number at risk") +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(), axis.line.y = element_blank(),
          plot.title = element_text(size = 11, margin = margin(b = 2)),
          plot.margin = margin(2, 5.5, 2, 5.5))
  list(plot = p, table = tab)
}

# Hazard-ratio (forest) plot for one factor of a Cox model: hazard ratios with robust 95% CIs (the model's
# genotype-clustered standard errors) and robust p-values; the reference level is shown at HR = 1.
hr_plot <- function(model, factor_name, labels) {
  s <- summary(model)
  ci <- s$conf.int; co <- s$coefficients
  rows <- grep(paste0("^", factor_name), rownames(ci))
  lv <- sub(paste0("^", factor_name), "", rownames(ci)[rows])
  ref <- setdiff(names(labels), lv)[1]
  d <- data.frame(level = c(ref, lv), HR = c(1, ci[rows, "exp(coef)"]),
                  lo = c(NA, ci[rows, "lower .95"]), hi = c(NA, ci[rows, "upper .95"]),
                  p = c(NA, co[rows, "Pr(>|z|)"]))
  d$label <- factor(labels[d$level], levels = rev(labels))
  d$txt <- ifelse(is.na(d$lo), "reference",
                  sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", d$HR, d$lo, d$hi))
  d$ptxt <- ifelse(is.na(d$p), "", ifelse(d$p < 0.001, "p < 0.001", sprintf("p = %s", formatC(signif(d$p, 2), digits = 2, format = "fg", flag = "#"))))
  rng <- range(c(d$lo, d$hi, 1), na.rm = TRUE)
  ci <- ggplot(d, aes(y = label, x = HR)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), width = 0.15, orientation = "y", na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_point(shape = 15, size = 3) +
    scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20), limits = c(rng[1] / 1.3, rng[2] * 1.3)) +
    labs(x = "Hazard ratio (robust 95% CI)", y = NULL) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
    theme(axis.line.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())
  # text columns (same rows): HR (95% CI) and robust p
  txt <- ggplot(d, aes(y = label)) +
    geom_text(aes(x = 0, label = txt), hjust = 0, size = 3.6) +
    geom_text(aes(x = 1, label = ptxt), hjust = 0, size = 3.6) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.6), breaks = c(0.35, 1.25), labels = c("HR (95% CI)", "p"), position = "top") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_void(base_size = 12) +
    theme(axis.text.x.top = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10), plot.margin = margin(5.5, 5.5, 25, 0))
  ggpubr::ggarrange(ci, txt, ncol = 2, widths = c(1.3, 1), align = "h")
}
```


# data import

```{r data-import}
urban <- read.csv("../../data/survivorship/urban survivorship.csv", head=T)

# fragments removed from the survivorship analysis (kept in the data file with the reason in 'exclude'):
# 31 O. faveolata that died from partial mortality unrelated to heat stress (mostly a ciliate infection;
# tissue loss without prior paling or bleaching), and one S. siderea with no health observations recorded.
# 'end' for these is the date the fragment was recorded dead
urban %>%
  filter(exclude != "") %>%
  count(species, treat, exclude)
urban <- urban %>% filter(exclude == "") %>% dplyr::select(-exclude)

# unique genotype ID (genotype numbers are nested within site and species)
urban$geno_id <- paste(urban$species, urban$site, urban$geno, sep = "_")

# second heat-stress cohort (control temperature fragments moved to heat): dates in the data file follow the
# tank loggers, which show the ambient tanks at 22.5 C through Apr 24 and at 24.0 C on Apr 28 23:15, reaching
# 33 C on May 10 (0.75 C/day): ramp 4/26, set point 5/10, seven days after the first cohort reached its set point
# (Apr 19); the control temperature period ends the day before (5/9). The file's `correction` column records the
# original schedule dates (ramp 4/23, set point 5/7, control end 5/6). Days are calculated from start and end.
urban %>%
  mutate(days = as.numeric(as.Date(end, "%m/%d/%y") - as.Date(start, "%m/%d/%y"))) -> urban
stopifnot(all(urban$days >= 0), !any(urban$ramp == "4/23/21"))
str(urban)
head(urban)

# Among the retained fragments, none died in the control temperature treatments (CC, LC) during the 20-day
# control period, so survival analyses use the heat treatments (CH, LH) only
urban %>%
  filter(treat %in% c("CC", "LC")) %>%
  group_by(species, treat) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), deaths = sum(status), days = max(days), .groups = "drop")

# Heat treatments combine two cohorts held in separate tanks: fragments heated from the start (4/5 ramp),
# and the control temperature fragments, which were moved to heat after the 20-day control period
# (4/26 ramp; CC -> CH, LC -> LH). Late-cohort LH fragments therefore had 3 additional weeks of
# low pH exposure before heat stress. Cohort effects are tested in the cohort and tank sensitivity section.
```


# survivorship by treatment

```{r survivorship-by-treatment}
# heat treatments only, by species
urban_ofav_treat <- subset(urban, species == "Ofav" & treat %in% c("CH", "LH"))
urban_ofav_treat$treat <- factor(urban_ofav_treat$treat, levels = c("CH", "LH"))
urban_ofav_treat$site <- factor(urban_ofav_treat$site, levels = c("Emerald", "Rainbow", "Star", "MacN"))

urban_ssid_treat <- subset(urban, species == "Ssid" & treat %in% c("CH", "LH"))
urban_ssid_treat$treat <- factor(urban_ssid_treat$treat, levels = c("CH", "LH"))
urban_ssid_treat$site <- factor(urban_ssid_treat$site, levels = c("Emerald", "Rainbow", "Star", "MacN"))

# Kaplan-Meier survival curves for each species
fit_ofav_treat <- survfit(Surv(days, status) ~ treat, data = urban_ofav_treat)
summary(fit_ofav_treat)

fit_ssid_treat <- survfit(Surv(days, status) ~ treat, data = urban_ssid_treat)
summary(fit_ssid_treat)

# display a Kaplan-Meier plot (survival curves + number-at-risk table) as a single figure
show_km <- function(p) ggarrange(p$plot, p$table, heights = c(2.2, 0.55), ncol = 1, nrow = 2)

# p-values for Kaplan-Meier plots: robust score (log-rank) test from the genotype-clustered Cox model
# always 2 significant figures, keeping trailing zeros (e.g. 0.080, not 0.08), so all panels show the same precision
robust_score_p <- function(model) {
  p <- unname(summary(model)$robscore["pvalue"])
  if (p < 0.001) return("p < 0.001")
  paste0("p = ", formatC(signif(p, 2), digits = 2, format = "fg", flag = "#"))
}

# Cox models use robust standard errors clustered by genotype (cluster = geno_id), because fragments from
# the same colony are not independent. p-values on the Kaplan-Meier plots are the genotype-adjusted
# robust score (log-rank) tests from these models.
# hazard ratio by treatment
hazard_ofav_treat <- coxph(Surv(days, status) ~ treat, data = urban_ofav_treat, cluster = geno_id)
summary(hazard_ofav_treat)

hazard_ssid_treat <- coxph(Surv(days, status) ~ treat, data = urban_ssid_treat, cluster = geno_id)
summary(hazard_ssid_treat)

# NOTE: hazard_ofav_treat violates the proportional hazards assumption (CH and LH survival curves cross
# near day 20), so its single hazard ratio in the plot below is not interpretable; the robust score test
# remains valid. See the O. faveolata time-split section for period-specific hazard ratios.

# Kaplan-Meier plots for each species
fill.color2<-c("#f4a582","#ca0020")
treat_labels <- c(CH = "Contemporary pH + Bleaching", LH = "Acidified + Bleaching")

survival_ofav_treat <- km_plot(fit_ofav_treat, pval = robust_score_p(hazard_ofav_treat), palette = fill.color2,
                               title = "Orbicella faveolata", labels = treat_labels, legend_title = "Treatment")
show_km(survival_ofav_treat)

survival_ssid_treat <- km_plot(fit_ssid_treat, pval = robust_score_p(hazard_ssid_treat), palette = fill.color2,
                               title = "Siderastrea siderea", labels = treat_labels, legend_title = "Treatment")
show_km(survival_ssid_treat)

# hazard ratio plots: robust (genotype-clustered) hazard ratios, 95% CIs and p-values; reference level at HR = 1
hazplot_ofav_treat <- hr_plot(hazard_ofav_treat, "treat", treat_labels)
hazplot_ofav_treat

hazplot_ssid_treat <- hr_plot(hazard_ssid_treat, "treat", treat_labels)
hazplot_ssid_treat

# survivorship by treatment figure
urban_treatment_multiplot<-ggarrange(survival_ofav_treat$plot,
                                     survival_ssid_treat$plot, 
                                     survival_ofav_treat$table, 
                                     survival_ssid_treat$table,
                                     hazplot_ofav_treat,
                                     hazplot_ssid_treat,
                                     heights = c(2.2, 0.42, 0.72),
                                     ncol = 2, nrow = 3)
urban_treatment_multiplot

ggsave("../../outputs/survivorship/urban survivorship treatment.pdf", urban_treatment_multiplot, width=10, height=8.5,dpi = 300)
```


# O. faveolata CH vs LH over time

```{r ofav-time-split}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The O. faveolata CH vs LH Cox model violates the proportional hazards
# assumption because the survival curves cross: LH delayed mortality until
# about day 20, then declined faster than CH. Splitting follow-up at day 20
# estimates a separate LH vs CH hazard ratio for each period.
# Hazards remain non-proportional after day 20 (cox.zph p < 0.01) because LH
# mortality is concentrated in days 20-27, so the after-day-20 hazard ratio is
# an average over that period; the direction (LH faster after day 20) is the
# robust conclusion.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
ofav_split <- survSplit(Surv(days, status) ~ treat + geno_id, data = urban_ofav_treat,
                        cut = 20, episode = "period") %>%
  mutate(LH_days_0_20 = as.numeric(treat == "LH" & period == 1),
         LH_after_day_20 = as.numeric(treat == "LH" & period == 2))

hazard_ofav_treat_split <- coxph(Surv(tstart, days, status) ~ LH_days_0_20 + LH_after_day_20,
                                 data = ofav_split, cluster = geno_id)
summary(hazard_ofav_treat_split)
cox.zph(hazard_ofav_treat_split) # proportional hazards within each period

s_split <- summary(hazard_ofav_treat_split)
ofav_time_split <- data.frame(period = c("days 0-20", "after day 20"),
                              LH_vs_CH_HR = round(s_split$conf.int[, 1], 2),
                              lower_95 = round(s_split$conf.int[, 3], 2),
                              upper_95 = round(s_split$conf.int[, 4], 2),
                              robust_p = signif(s_split$coefficients[, "Pr(>|z|)"], 3))
ofav_time_split

write.csv(ofav_time_split, file = "../../outputs/survivorship/urban survivorship ofav treatment time split.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r survivorship-by-site}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CH vs LH survival did not differ in either species, so the heat treatments
# are combined for site comparisons, using the same datasets as the treatment
# section. Cox models are stratified by treatment, giving CH and LH separate
# baseline hazards (O. faveolata CH and LH survival curves cross), and use

# Kaplan-Meier survival curves for each species

summary(fit_ssid_site)

# hazard ratio by site
hazard_ofav_site <- coxph(Surv(days, status) ~ site + strata(treat), data = urban_ofav_treat, cluster = geno_id)
summary(hazard_ofav_site)

hazard_ssid_site <- coxph(Surv(days, status) ~ site + strata(treat), data = urban_ssid_treat, cluster = geno_id)

site_labels <- c(Emerald = "Emerald Reef", Rainbow = "Rainbow Reef", Star = "Star Island", MacN = "MacArthur North")

hazplot_ofav_site <- hr_plot(hazard_ofav_site, "site", site_labels)
hazplot_ofav_site

hazplot_ssid_site <- hr_plot(hazard_ssid_site, "site", site_labels)
hazplot_ssid_site

# survivorship by site figure
urban_site_multiplot<-ggarrange(survival_ofav_site$plot,
                                survival_ssid_site$plot, 
                                survival_ofav_site$table, 
                                survival_ssid_site$table,

                                hazplot_ssid_site,
                                heights = c(2.2, 0.55, 0.95),
                                ncol = 2, nrow = 3)
urban_site_multiplot

ggsave("../../outputs/survivorship/urban survivorship site.pdf", urban_site_multiplot, width=10, height=9.5,dpi = 300)
```


# urban vs reef contrast

```{r urban-reef-contrast}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Planned contrast from the site Cox models (stratified by treatment, robust SEs
# clustered by genotype): mean log hazard of the urban sites (Star Island,
# MacArthur North) minus the mean of the reef sites (Emerald, Rainbow).
# Emerald is the reference level (coefficient 0), so the weights on the site
# coefficients are Rainbow -0.5, Star +0.5, MacN +0.5. HR < 1 = lower hazard
# for urban-origin corals.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
urban_reef_cox <- function(model) {
  b <- coef(model)
  w <- c(siteRainbow = -0.5, siteStar = 0.5, siteMacN = 0.5)[names(b)]
  stopifnot(!anyNA(w))
  est <- sum(w * b)
  se  <- sqrt(drop(t(w) %*% vcov(model) %*% w)) # vcov() is the robust (clustered) covariance
  z   <- est / se
  data.frame(contrast = "urban - reef", log_HR = est, robust_se = se,
             HR = exp(est), HR_lower95 = exp(est - 1.96 * se), HR_upper95 = exp(est + 1.96 * se),
             z = z, p = 2 * pnorm(-abs(z)))
}

urban_reef_surv <- bind_rows(
  cbind(species = "Ofav", urban_reef_cox(hazard_ofav_site)),
  cbind(species = "Ssid", urban_reef_cox(hazard_ssid_site)))
urban_reef_surv

write.csv(urban_reef_surv, file = "../../outputs/survivorship/urban survivorship urban reef contrasts.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```


# days to mortality

```{r days-to-mortality}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# All fragments in the heat treatments died (no censoring), so mean days to
# mortality is exact. Control temperature treatments had no mortality and are
# excluded. Days are counted from the end of the temperature ramp (start date).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
sem <- function(x) sd(x) / sqrt(length(x))

urban_heat <- urban %>%
  filter(treat %in% c("CH", "LH")) %>%
  mutate(site = factor(site, levels = c("Emerald", "Rainbow", "Star", "MacN")))

days_summary <- function(dat, grouping, ...) {
  dat %>%
    group_by(species, ...) %>%
    summarise(n = n(), deaths = sum(status), mean_days = round(mean(days), 2),
              sem_days = round(sem(days), 2), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(grouping = grouping, .after = species)
}

days_to_mortality <- bind_rows(
  days_summary(urban_heat, "treatment", treat),
  days_summary(urban_heat, "site", site),
  days_summary(urban_heat, "treatment x site", treat, site)
) %>%
  dplyr::select(species, grouping, treat, site, everything()) %>%
  mutate(grouping = factor(grouping, levels = c("treatment", "site", "treatment x site"))) %>%
  arrange(species, grouping, treat, site)
days_to_mortality

write.csv(days_to_mortality, file = "../../outputs/survivorship/urban survivorship days to mortality.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```


# model outputs and proportional hazards testing

```{r model-outputs}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Exports hazard ratios, model tests, and proportional hazards tests for all
# Cox models. Models use robust standard errors clustered by genotype, so the
# robust Wald and robust score tests are the genotype-adjusted tests to report;
# the likelihood ratio and log-rank tests assume independent fragments.
# Proportional hazards: cox.zph() p-values below 0.05 indicate the hazard ratio
# changes over time, so a single hazard ratio is not a valid summary; in that
# case, report the robust score (log-rank) test instead.
# O. faveolata CH vs LH (hazard_ofav_treat) violates this assumption.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
cox_models <- list(ofav_treat = hazard_ofav_treat, ssid_treat = hazard_ssid_treat,
                   ofav_treat_time_split = hazard_ofav_treat_split,
                   ofav_site = hazard_ofav_site, ssid_site = hazard_ssid_site)

# proportional hazards tests
lapply(cox_models, cox.zph)

capture.output({
  for (nm in names(cox_models)) {
    s <- summary(cox_models[[nm]])
    cat("=== ", nm, " ===\n", sep = "")
    cat("n =", s$n, " events =", s$nevent, "\n")
    print(round(s$conf.int, 3))
    print(signif(s$coefficients, 3))
    cat("Genotype-adjusted tests: robust Wald p =", signif(s$waldtest["pvalue"], 3),
        " robust score p =", signif(s$robscore["pvalue"], 3), "\n")
    cat("Unadjusted tests: likelihood ratio p =", signif(s$logtest["pvalue"], 3),
        " log-rank p =", signif(s$sctest["pvalue"], 3), "\n")
    cat("Proportional hazards test (cox.zph):\n")
    print(cox.zph(cox_models[[nm]])$table)
    cat("\n")
  }
}, file = "../../outputs/survivorship/urban survivorship stats.txt")
```


# genotype effects

```{r genotype-effects}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Genotype is the main source of variation in time to mortality under heat
# stress. Because genotypes are nested within sites, the replicates for site
# comparisons are genotypes, not fragments.
#   1. variance partitioning: days ~ treatment + site + cohort + (1 | genotype)
#      (all heat fragments died, so days to mortality is uncensored)
#   2. consistency of genotype responses across CH and LH (correlation of genotype means)
#   3. site comparison using genotype means as replicates
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
geno_heat <- urban_heat %>%
  mutate(cohort = if_else(ramp == "4/5/21", "early ramp", "late ramp"),
         treat = factor(treat, levels = c("CH", "LH")))

geno_results <- lapply(c("Ofav", "Ssid"), function(sp) {
  d <- filter(geno_heat, species == sp)

  # 1. variance partitioning, with LRT for the genotype random effect
  m <- lmer(days ~ treat + site + cohort + (1 | geno_id), data = d, REML = TRUE)
  m0 <- lm(days ~ treat + site + cohort, data = d)
  vc <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(m))
  lrt <- 2 * (as.numeric(logLik(update(m, REML = FALSE))) - as.numeric(logLik(m0)))

  # 2. genotype means in CH vs LH, for genotypes present in both
  g_trt <- d %>%
    group_by(geno_id, treat) %>%
    summarise(mean_days = mean(days), .groups = "drop") %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = treat, values_from = mean_days) %>%
    filter(!is.na(CH), !is.na(LH))
  ct <- cor.test(g_trt$CH, g_trt$LH)

  # 3. site comparison on genotype means
  g_site <- d %>%
    group_by(geno_id, site) %>%
    summarise(mean_days = mean(days), .groups = "drop")
  site_means <- tapply(g_site$mean_days, g_site$site, mean)

  data.frame(species = sp,
             genotype_pct_nonfixed_var = round(100 * vc$vcov[vc$grp == "geno_id"] / sum(vc$vcov), 1),
             genotype_LRT_p = signif(pchisq(lrt, 1, lower.tail = FALSE) / 2, 3), # halved: variance tested at boundary of zero
             n_geno_both_treatments = nrow(g_trt),
             CH_LH_genotype_r = round(unname(ct$estimate), 2),
             CH_LH_genotype_r_p = signif(ct$p.value, 3),
             n_geno = nrow(g_site),
             t(setNames(round(site_means, 2), paste0("mean_days_geno_", names(site_means)))),
             site_anova_p = signif(summary(aov(mean_days ~ site, data = g_site))[[1]][["Pr(>F)"]][1], 3),
             site_kruskal_p = signif(kruskal.test(mean_days ~ site, data = g_site)$p.value, 3))
})
genotype_effects <- bind_rows(geno_results)
genotype_effects

write.csv(genotype_effects, file = "../../outputs/survivorship/urban survivorship genotype effects.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```


# cohort and tank sensitivity

```{r cohort-sensitivity}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Each heat treatment combines two cohorts held in separate tanks: fragments
# heated from the start (4/5 ramp) and the control temperature fragments (CC, LC),
# moved to heat after the 20-day control period (4/26 ramp). Tests whether cohort (equivalent to tank within
# treatment) affects survival, and whether adjusting for it changes the
# treatment or site results. All models clustered by genotype; p-values are
# robust score tests, except the treatment x cohort interaction (robust Wald).
# Stratifying by tank also stratifies by treatment, since tanks are nested in
# treatment.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
cohort_results <- lapply(c("Ofav", "Ssid"), function(sp) {
  d <- filter(geno_heat, species == sp)
  rscore <- function(m) signif(summary(m)$robscore["pvalue"], 3)
  hr <- function(m) round(summary(m)$conf.int[1, 1], 2)

  m_cohort   <- coxph(Surv(days, status) ~ cohort, data = d, cluster = geno_id)
  m_int      <- coxph(Surv(days, status) ~ treat * cohort, data = d, cluster = geno_id)
  m_trt      <- coxph(Surv(days, status) ~ treat, data = d, cluster = geno_id)
  m_trt_str  <- coxph(Surv(days, status) ~ treat + strata(cohort), data = d, cluster = geno_id)
  m_site     <- coxph(Surv(days, status) ~ site + strata(treat), data = d, cluster = geno_id)
  m_site_str <- coxph(Surv(days, status) ~ site + strata(tank), data = d, cluster = geno_id)
  int_row    <- grep(":", rownames(summary(m_int)$coefficients))

  data.frame(species = sp,
             cohort_p = rscore(m_cohort),
             treat_x_cohort_p = signif(summary(m_int)$coefficients[int_row, "Pr(>|z|)"], 3),
             LH_vs_CH_HR = hr(m_trt), LH_vs_CH_p = rscore(m_trt),
             LH_vs_CH_HR_cohort_strata = hr(m_trt_str), LH_vs_CH_p_cohort_strata = rscore(m_trt_str),
             site_p = rscore(m_site), site_p_tank_strata = rscore(m_site_str))
})
cohort_sensitivity <- bind_rows(cohort_results)
cohort_sensitivity

write.csv(cohort_sensitivity, file = "../../outputs/survivorship/urban survivorship cohort sensitivity.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```
